name: Temporary Resident Visa

requirements.blocker_text: Requires bank statements showing an average monthly balance over USD 42,164 (12 months of statements), OR proof of employment/pension income exceeding USD 2,530/month (6 months of statements). Figures are consular conversions of a legal threshold denominated in days of Mexico City's general minimum wage, so exact USD/MXN amounts shift over time.
Requires ownership of Mexican real property valued at over USD 337,308 (or MXN 6,914,800), evidenced by a public deed.
Requires shares in a Mexican corporation where the amount effectively disbursed for the foreigner's shares exceeds USD 168,654 (or MXN 3,457,000).
requirements.fix_path: Fund and document the qualifying share investment.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires either company property exceeding USD 168,654 (MXN 3,457,000), or a documented, operating business employing at least 3 people.

Non-remunerated participation with institutional sponsorship: if the inviting institution covers expenses, requires an average monthly balance of USD 84,327; if self-funded, requires USD 42,164 average balance or USD 1,687/month income.

evidence_required.document: Bank statements or income/pension documentation (per group)
Property deed, share certificates, or business registration (per group)

outcome.duration_length: more than 180 days, less than 4 years (visa-holder chooses initial validity within this range, renewable within the 4-year cap)

sources.title: Consulate of Mexico, Phoenix (SRE) -- Temporary Resident visa: qualifying categories and thresholds

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Mexico's initial build. FIVE GENUINELY DIFFERENT QUALIFYING GROUNDS modelled as OR-logic groups for the SAME visa (Temporary Resident) rather than split into separate route files -- the source presents them explicitly as alternative categories of one visa. work_rights set 'none': this consular economic/property-based temporary resident visa does not itself confer work authorisation -- employment requires the separate employer-sponsored route (mx_work_permit_employer_sponsored) or a subsequent permission change. Family-unity is a genuinely distinct, separately-documented visa (its own trámite, own eligible-relatives list, and an outcome that can itself be permanent residence) and is modelled as its own file, mx_family_unity_visa, rather than as a sixth group here. pr_after_months set to 48 based on the standard time-based change-of-status rule (see mx_permanent_residence_via_temporary); citizenship_after_months (60) reflects that naturalisation additionally requires its own residence count from mx_naturalisation_residence, not confirmed here as automatically cumulative with the PR wait.
